items.title: Add a `--suffix` option to `uv tool install`
items.reason: Canonical request for multiple installations of the same tool under distinct names. Maintainer comments describe suffixes as part of installation identity and applying them to every entry point. The proposed --alias spelling and editable-versus-published example refine the same capability.

items.title: allow multiple installations of a tool with different names in the bin folder
items.reason: Requested separately named installations of the same package with different plugin dependencies. A maintainer closed it as a duplicate of astral-sh/uv#6365, and the reporter agreed, establishing that the canonical request includes independent environments rather than executable renaming alone.

items.title: Add suffix support to tool installs
items.reason: Open draft targeting astral-sh/uv#6365. Proposes suffix-based installation identities, renaming every entry point, retaining package identity in receipts, and supporting list, upgrade, and uninstall. Predates this report and remains unmerged; it proposes suffixes rather than arbitrary aliases.

items.title: Add --suffix option to uv tool install (astral-sh/uv#6365)
items.reason: Another open, unmerged implementation targeting astral-sh/uv#6365. Its description covers coexisting installations, suffixed entry points, package/suffix receipt fields, and management commands resolving suffixed names. Predates this report and uses suffixes rather than arbitrary aliases.

items.title: [WIP] Add a `--suffix` option to `uv tool install`
items.reason: Earlier implementation for astral-sh/uv#6365, closed without merging. It separated environments by package plus suffix; maintainer review discussed retaining the underlying package name for upgrades and handling executable extensions. Its closure does not establish a shipped feature or regression.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs with authenticated gh. Separate literal searches covered --alias, uv tool install, editable installations, different sources, tool list/upgrade/uninstall, and entry-point collisions. Conceptual searches covered suffixes, renaming, multiple versions/installations, side-by-side tools, independent environments, and area:uv-tool. Followed astral-sh/uv#6365 comments and timeline to its prior duplicate, implementation PRs, and the design in astral-sh/uv#3560; inspected PR comments and reviews. PR keyword searches returned no matches, so linked PRs were retrieved directly and their states verified; no merged implementation was identified. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#14118, which concerns project command aliases, and astral-sh/uv#15384, which concerns project-specific tool version selection. Checked the current CLI and package-keyed tool storage separately from capability searches.

type_reason: The independently managed, separately named installations requested here are already tracked by open astral-sh/uv#6365. The prior duplicate astral-sh/uv#12451 and pre-existing implementation proposals explicitly cover separate dependency environments and lifecycle commands. Arbitrary aliases and editable-versus-published installations are additional design details, and the reporter allows alternative interfaces. No prior merged implementation or regression is established; duplicate takes precedence over enhancement.
summary: astral-sh/uv#6365 is the canonical discussion. astral-sh/uv#12451 establishes a closely matching duplicate precedent; astral-sh/uv#20370 and astral-sh/uv#21272 are open implementation proposals, while astral-sh/uv#7095 closed unmerged.
draft_response: Your goal of independently managing multiple installations of one package is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#6365 through a proposed `--suffix` option. The proposal covers distinct names for each entry point, and astral-sh/uv#20370 and astral-sh/uv#21272 propose corresponding `list`, `upgrade`, and `uninstall` support; both remain unmerged. Please continue in astral-sh/uv#6365 with your editable-versus-published example and preference for arbitrary aliases so those details can inform the shared design.
